name: Any Day
tagline: Nobody you love ever has to ask you. They only have to mention it.
epigraph: Ordered after a long shift: the usual, with honey instead of sugar. Now it's a classic.
glassware: rocks glass, one large plain cube (the biggest cube your freezer makes; not clear, not cut)

names_note: **Any Day**, the room's pick (all three, round 5): the bartender's line in y5 ("I'd do this for you any day" is plenty), so ordering the drink means saying it once. It's never Siegal's words. **The Plumber's Coming** was Tomás's pick until round 5: the unmade ask, heard. It's a paraphrase of p. 88, never in quote marks, and Siegal's naming rule (no "connection to the origin of the drink") leans against it because it's drawn from the story. Also considered: *Thirty Copies* (three thirties in one pour), *The Other Eighteen*, *Heard You*.
open_items: **History share** is about 54% of yours (38% of the whole reading), at the limit. Wren flagged it herself: if Robin wants it lower, the chalkboard sentence (Union Square Cafe) goes first.

**The thirty copies** (p. 93): the page partly cuts against us (they follow "Siegal didn't agree", and Proper calls him an investor, p. 113). The reading grants the sceptic in the same paragraph ("Maybe it was just good for business.") and signposts the pride once. The thirty-seconds and thirty-copies coincidence is owned in y4 ("Thirty again: a coincidence, nothing more.").

**The drink uses a third less honey syrup than the printed recipe** (15 ml against ¾ oz): the printed ¾ oz of 3:1 reads OUT on sugar (12.19 g/100 ml). y4 owns the change. The measures are the printed recipe's, and Siegal's order was the idea (bourbon sour, honey instead of sugar).

**The bottle:** Elijah Craig Small Batch (Proper's "single batch" read as a slip; *PUNCH* has Knob Creek the first night, then Elijah Craig 12). Today's Small Batch is younger whiskey under the same name (no age statement since January 2016), so it's never "the bourbon they used". The 47% is unsourced, and the sweep from 40 to 50% balances.

**Kept out on purpose:** Petraske's rules, genius, hand-carved ice and death; money as the guest's scene (*Next One's Mine*); ginger (the Penicillin and Siegal's own Ginger Gold Rush); Toby Maloney's hand in the house syrup (dossier only); any year for the drink (*PUNCH* "sometime in 2000" against Proper's 2001).
**Image brief colour** ("hazy pale amber-gold") is Tomás's read. No page describes the drink's colour.
